title: Maximum Number of Alloys
summary: You manage a company that produces alloys using various metal types.
statement: You manage a company that produces alloys using various metal types. With n metal types, k machines are available, each needing a specific amount of each metal to produce an alloy. You start with stock units of each metal, and purchasing additional units costs a certain number of coins. Given the number of metal types, machines, budget, and details on composition and stock, determine the maximum number of alloys that can be produced without exceeding the budget. All alloys must be made using the same machine.
constraints: n is the number of metals, k is the number of machine recipes, and dimensions agree.
All alloys use one chosen machine; missing units may be purchased at per-metal costs within budget.
Return the maximum number of alloys one machine can produce.
hints: For one recipe, purchase cost grows monotonically with the alloy count.
Binary-search each machine’s maximum affordable count, then take the best.
Compute missing units max(0,count*need-stock), multiply by costs, and expand an upper bound before binary search.
Monotone affordability makes the last true count exact for each machine, and the outer maximum enforces the single-machine choice.
editorial: Monotone affordability makes the last true count exact for each machine, and the outer maximum enforces the single-machine choice.

tests.explanation: The first recipe produces two alloys for twelve coins, while a third exceeds budget.
Stocked third metal lets the second machine produce five alloys for fifteen coins.
